name: Resultadismo / pragmatism
scopeNote: Resultadismo (Spanish; Solari in El Pais: the word 'no figura en el diccionario') or pragmatism, in Brazilian terms 'futebol de resultados' as opposed to 'futebol d'arte' (The Conversation): result over style, with the system and block chosen to suit squad and opponent. It is a stance, not a shape: sources show Capello changing 4-4-2 / 3-4-1-2 / 4-3-3 / 4-2-3-1 by squad, Scolari moving a 3-5-2 to 3-3-3-1 and 3-4-2-1 by match, Deschamps using 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3 / 3-4-1-2 with a deep block and counters. Period runs from Capello's first Milan season (1991, month only: exact appointment and exit dates not checked) to Deschamps' 2022 World Cup (final 2022-12-18); Scolari 2002 World Cup sits between. Popular label caution: 'catenaccio' or 'defensive' is not the same thing; Capello's Milan kept the Sacchi 4-4-2 and zonal base but dropped the full-pitch press (Holding Midfield), and Edmilson says Scolari's three centre-backs were meant to raise attacking volume. Resultadismo is also used in Argentina/Spain as a pejorative for short-termism (Perfil, Solari), a different sense not profiled here. No tier A source found; marking system of these sides not covered by a verified page (Capello wrote a 1984 Coverciano paper on zonal marking per search summary only).
openQuestions: Is 'resultadismo' a tactical ideology at all? Solari (El Pais) questions the word itself and notes it can mean defensive, rigid, elastic or not interested in possession; we use it as 'result first, adapt to opponent/squad'.

Scolari 2002 pragmatism label: Edmilson says the 3-5-2 was to add attacking volume, Lucio says defensive security, a Brazilian academic piece called it overly defensive; sources disagree on the motive.
Capello Milan marking (zonal vs mixed) and Scolari/Deschamps marking not verified by any page read; Deschamps' 2012-2026 spell dates and Scolari's exact World Cup spell dates not checked.
Deschamps himself says (Orange/Figaro 2025, search summary only) that without play you cannot win over time, which contradicts the 'only victory' label; not verified.

sources.title: The pragmatic success story of Fabio Capello

sources.title: The pragmatic success story of Fabio Capello

sources.title: 12 Greatest Club Sides: 8) AC Milan 1991-96
